source.read: Entire uploaded UX audit plus both inline stress/scroll reports. Author findings treated as hypotheses to reproduce, not agent runtime evidence. Some cases already partly addressed in unreleased work.

requirements.title: Large imports within advertised limits never overflow the JS argument stack
requirements.source: 2026-10-19 user stress/scroll report and pasted UX audit
acceptance: Import10000x20 and10000x30 numeric tables, navigate/edit/plot/save/reopen without blank page or stack overflow; calculate bounds by iteration.
implementation_evidence: gp/models.py: AnalysisRequest accepts at most 30 columns, 10,000 values per column and 300,000 total cells, matching the advertised table dimensions.
web/src/plot-geometry.ts computes bounds by iteration; dense graphs use a full-observation canvas and inactive graphs unmount.
validation_evidence: tests/test_table_capacity.py: server API fully analyzes 10,000x30 column and XY tables and verifies n, mean, sample SD and sum; rejects 10,000x31, 10,001x30 and individual dimension overflows.

2026-10-19: capacity, API and edge subset passed 38 tests. Native 300,000-cell descriptive probe: validation 0.147 s, analysis 0.236 s, whole-process peak RSS 93.4 MiB including Python/SciPy imports; not a browser performance guarantee.
2026-10-19 parent integration report: full backend suite passed 266 tests. Unit/server validation only; no native Prism equivalence or static/browser completion inferred.
plot-geometry.test.ts exercises 200,000 and 300,000 observations; standalone Chromium rendered all 200,000 observations with 82 Plot DOM nodes and no page errors.
Server Chromium completed200k/300k import/full drawing and zoom isolation; evidence in /workspace/gp-evidence/large-workbook-capacity.json, with explicit two-run scope and timing limitations.
limitations: Server Chromium import, navigation and full drawing passed for 200,000/300,000 observations. Full-capacity static-worker calculation and complete edit/save/reopen acceptance remain open; smaller static integration tests do not prove these cases.
Server graph export retains its separately declared 20,000-cell rendering limit.
Large-table editing still incurs whole-workbook serialization/history costs, tracked in B005.

requirements.title: Render recovery preserves downloadable current work
requirements.source: 2026-10-19 user stress/scroll report and pasted UX audit
acceptance: Unexpected render errors show recovery actions and meaningful diagnostics; download latest in-memory workbook; never clear or overwrite saved original during recovery.
implementation_evidence: Global React boundary retains latest immutable workbook reference, offers download and retry, and leaves saved storage unchanged.
validation_evidence: Server and static Chromium injected a render error after an unsaved edit; download and Retry preserved latest values/name, and previous browser save remained unchanged.

requirements.title: Numeric-domain limits and useful Python errors
requirements.source: 2026-10-19 user stress/scroll report and pasted UX audit
acceptance: Frontend/server/static enforce finite absolute values≤1e100; reject1e200 with field/row reason; no bare Pydantic URL or module prefix.
implementation_evidence: gp/models.py and gp/server.py: finite absolute observation limit is inclusively 1e100; validation returns concise JSON messages without raw input or Pydantic URL/context echoes.
web/src/data.ts: numeric(), importCsv(), requestData() and project validation enforce the same numeric bound with row/column context where available.
web/src/error-message.ts and web/src/compute.worker.ts: structured or traceback errors retain meaningful constraints and strip module/URL noise; worker uses the shared error formatter.
validation_evidence: tests/test_analysis_edges.py: analyze/export reject both signs of 1e101, 1e200 and 1e308; exactly +/-1e100 is accepted with known sample SD; hostile names remain literal JSON data and escaped SVG text.

web/src/data.test.ts and web/src/error-message.test.ts: cap boundaries, row/column locations, Pydantic footer removal, structured errors and hostile React text tested. Combined Node test command passed all 19 tests on 2026-10-19.
2026-10-19 parent integration report: full backend suite passed 266 tests. Unit/server validation only; no native Prism equivalence or static/browser completion inferred.

Server and static Chromium checks displayed meaningful constant-data and 1e200 errors without module prefixes or Pydantic footer text; scripts/check_large_workbook.py and /workspace/gp-evidence/large-workbook-static-integration.json.
limitations: The 1e100 bound is a GP resource/numerical policy, not an inferred Prism numeric-domain limit.

requirements.title: Independent imported-table defaults
requirements.source: 2026-10-19 user stress/scroll report and pasted UX audit
acceptance: CSV/native imports start with own name/title, neutral labels and descriptive analysis; unrelated current sheet settings never leak.
implementation_evidence: CSV and native imports use importedProject with independent labels, title, analysis and graph defaults.
validation_evidence: data.test.ts fresh-import isolation and semicolon cases; integrated200k/300k import checks confirmed neutral own settings.

requirements.title: Virtualized large grid
requirements.source: 2026-10-19 user stress/scroll report and pasted UX audit
acceptance: Only visible rows/columns plus overscan mounted; editing row10000 in30columns retains data and focus; measure mounted node count and edit latency.
implementation_evidence: DataGrid.tsx virtualizes rows and columns, retaining a maximum of 80 data rows including offscreen focus.
validation_evidence: 19 Chromium grid workflows passed; 42 mounted rows on a 10,000-row table. Last cell AD10000 persisted through reload.
limitations: Editing still incurs whole-workbook serialization/history costs. Measured production latency under host contention was 429–678ms for typical 8-column edits and 829–2543ms for 30 columns; virtualization alone does not resolve end-to-end lag.

requirements.title: Dense graph rendering without one DOM node per point
requirements.source: 2026-10-19 user stress/scroll report and pasted UX audit
acceptance: Render all observations with bounded DOM/canvas, no silent statistical/data subsampling; preserve full bounds, summaries and exports.
implementation_evidence: All dense observations draw on high-resolution canvas; summary/fit/axes remain SVG.
validation_evidence: 13 geometry/selection regressions; actual painted canvas and 200,000-point spatial hit testing verified in Chromium.
limitations: Native visual fidelity and dense graph exports remain separate requirements.

requirements.title: Spreadsheet keyboard and replacement editing
requirements.source: 2026-10-19 user stress/scroll report and pasted UX audit
acceptance: Click selects cell; typing replaces; F2/doubleclick edits; Enter/ShiftEnter and arrows move rows, Tab/ShiftTab columns with correct boundaries.
implementation_evidence: Selected-cell and caret editing modes; Enter/ShiftEnter/Tab/arrows/F2 navigation.
validation_evidence: Chromium replacement typing, keyboard movement, F2, missing cells and offscreen focus checks passed.
Final review: selected-mode Ctrl/Cmd+Z reverses range clear/paste, while caret editing retains native text history; six focused browser regressions passed with zero page errors.
limitations: Subcolumn/replicate-specific Prism navigation remains pending typed-table work.

requirements.title: Samples and table-format changes do not silently overwrite
requirements.source: 2026-10-19 user stress/scroll report and pasted UX audit
acceptance: Sample workflows add a new table or explicitly confirm replacement; format changes are deliberate, undoable and describe reinterpretation.
implementation_evidence: Choosing a sample adds a new data table instead of overwriting the current one.
validation_evidence: Shared addData workbook helper is tested; sample-specific browser workflow and explicit table-format dialog remain open.

requirements.title: Stable analysis identity and isolated parameters
requirements.source: 2026-10-19 user stress/scroll report and pasted UX audit
acceptance: Repeat identical analysis reuses the appropriate result; explicit new creates unique name; parameter changes affect result only and update generated titles without overwriting custom names.
implementation_evidence: Ordinary Run reuses matching result identity; explicit Create analysis remains independent; result parameter changes preserve source settings and rename default labels.
validation_evidence: Server and static Chromium verified reuse, explicit new identity, unchanged sibling/source settings, and default result renaming.

requirements.title: Scientific number and label formatting
requirements.source: 2026-10-19 user stress/scroll report and pasted UX audit
acceptance: Large/small magnitudes use readable scientific notation;0.99997 never displays as1; EC50 casing correct; stored/full-precision values unchanged.
implementation_evidence: gp/statistics.py: standalone 4PL parameter result label is explicitly EC50.
web/src/data.ts: fmt() uses scientific notation for |x|>=1e6 or 0<|x|<0.001; preserves near-integer distinctions such as 0.99997; formatting returns text without mutating stored values.
validation_evidence: tests/test_analysis_edges.py: known 4PL fixture verifies the EC50 label and value and rejects the old Ec50 label.

web/src/data.test.ts: checks positive/negative 1e100, large/small notation boundaries, null/nonfinite formatting and near-one values down to 0.9999999999999999. Included in the 19 passing Node tests on 2026-10-19.
2026-10-19 parent integration report: full backend suite passed 266 tests. Unit/server validation only; no native Prism equivalence or static/browser completion inferred.
limitations: Rendered browser/static result presentation and persistence/full-precision export roundtrips for these cases remain to be exercised.
Numeric presentation thresholds are explicit GP choices; no Prism visual equivalence is claimed.

requirements.title: XY descriptive statistics exclude X by default
requirements.source: 2026-10-19 user stress/scroll report and pasted UX audit
acceptance: Y series alone appear in descriptive summary; X missingness does not drop independent Y observations unless paired analysis requires it.
implementation_evidence: gp/statistics.py: descriptive XY analysis summarizes Y columns only, independently retains Y observations when X is missing, and reports that missing-X rule in method notes.
validation_evidence: tests/test_analysis_edges.py: synthetic missing-X/missing-Y fixture checks Y-only names, independent counts, known means and sum; an XY table with only X observations fails explicitly.
tests/test_table_capacity.py: 10,000x30 XY input returns exactly 29 Y summaries with analytically known descriptive outputs.
2026-10-19 parent integration report: full backend suite passed 266 tests. Unit/server validation only; no native Prism equivalence or static/browser completion inferred.
limitations: Static-worker/browser rendering and saved result roundtrip verification are pending; native Prism behavior has not been exercised for this edge case.

requirements.title: Paired Hedges correction undefined for two pairs
requirements.source: 2026-10-19 user stress/scroll report and pasted UX audit
acceptance: For n2, g is null with explicit df≤1 reason; valid paired inference remains unchanged and no false zero effect reported.
implementation_evidence: gp/statistics.py: paired Hedges g is null for two complete pairs (residual df=1), with an explicit fewer-than-three-pairs bias-correction reason; paired t, Cohen d, direction and valid inference remain available.
validation_evidence: tests/test_analysis_edges.py: two-pair differences [1,3] give df=1, t=2 and Cohen d=sqrt(2), while Hedges g is null with an explanatory warning.
tests/test_prism_reference.py: existing larger-sample paired saved-output regression remains passing; it is not a Prism reference for n=2.
2026-10-19 parent integration report: full backend suite passed 266 tests. Unit/server validation only; no native Prism equivalence or static/browser completion inferred.
limitations: Static-worker/browser visibility and serialization of the undefined result remain pending.
Existing df>1 approximation is unchanged; this correction does not add an exact gamma-function Hedges correction or infer Prism n=2 behavior.

requirements.title: Per-series dose-response failures
requirements.source: 2026-10-19 user stress/scroll report and pasted UX audit
acceptance: One constant-Y series produces named failure while valid series still fit; all-invalid inputs give a clear overall failure; no series silently disappears.
implementation_evidence: gp/statistics.py: standalone dose_response 4PL skips an unidentifiable constant-Y series only after recording its named Fit status and warning; valid series still fit. If every Y series is constant, an aggregate AnalysisError names each failed series.
validation_evidence: tests/test_analysis_edges.py: constant series before/after a known valid curve retains the valid EC50=5 fit, named failure status and warning; one/all-constant series return explicit overall failure, including a 422 API response.
2026-10-19 parent integration report: full backend suite passed 266 tests. Unit/server validation only; no native Prism equivalence or static/browser completion inferred.
limitations: Bounded implementation handles constant-Y failure in standalone 4PL only. Invalid X, insufficient pairs, optimizer nonconvergence and nonlinear-registry failures retain prior whole-request error behavior; no universal per-series recovery is claimed.
Static-worker/browser presentation and result persistence for mixed/all-invalid series remain pending.

requirements.title: No-event logrank undefined explanation
requirements.source: 2026-10-19 user stress/scroll report and pasted UX audit
acceptance: No observed events produce explicit undefined result/reason visible in UI; never imply df0 is a successful test.
implementation_evidence: gp/survival.py: logrank returns status=undefined, null statistic/p value and an explicit no-events undefined_reason; warnings propagate at both comparison and overall survival response levels. df=0 remains the covariance rank, not a successful test.
validation_evidence: tests/test_analysis_edges.py and tests/test_survival.py: all-censored synthetic groups produce no-event reason, null inference, rank zero and warnings at both levels; saved Prism event-bearing logrank regression remains passing.
2026-10-19 parent integration report: full backend suite passed 266 tests. Unit/server validation only; no native Prism equivalence or static/browser completion inferred.
limitations: Explicit UI visibility and static-worker runtime acceptance remain pending; current frontend source renders warnings but still displays rank zero, so source inspection alone does not close this obligation.
No native Prism runtime no-event reference has been obtained; event-bearing saved-output agreement does not verify this undefined edge.

requirements.title: Prominent browser-storage failure and recovery
requirements.source: 2026-10-19 user stress/scroll report and pasted UX audit
acceptance: Quota failure immediately exposes persistent warning, download and retry; later edits remain downloadable; saved original preserved; recovery re-enables save visibly.
implementation_evidence: Persistent storage-failure alert offers current-workbook download/retry; unsaved changes warn before page exit.
validation_evidence: Server and static Chromium injected quota failure, confirmed saved bytes unchanged and latest value17 in downloaded workbook.

requirements.title: Semicolon CSV with quoting/BOM/CRLF
requirements.source: 2026-10-19 user stress/scroll report and pasted UX audit
acceptance: Detect comma/semicolon outside quotes; numeric values and hostile titles roundtrip; mixed delimiters fail clearly.
implementation_evidence: Main CSV import autodetects semicolon or comma outside quotes; export preserves quoted/missing cells.
validation_evidence: 14 data unit cases and server and static Chromium semicolon hostile-name fixture passed.

requirements.title: Messages do not shift grid; transient notices expire
requirements.source: 2026-10-19 user stress/scroll report and pasted UX audit
acceptance: Errors/storage warnings remain accessible in fixed overlay/slot; opening/closing messages cannot move clicked cell; copy success expires, real failures persist.
implementation_evidence: Success notices expire after5seconds; errors and persistent save warnings overlay rather than shift the grid.
validation_evidence: Server and static Chromium constant-input and overflow failures kept identical grid top coordinates; timing-specific notice expiry remains to verify.

requirements.title: Sticky row headers
requirements.source: 2026-10-19 user stress/scroll report and pasted UX audit
acceptance: Horizontal scrolling keeps numbered row header visible with opaque background and correct stacking under fixed column headers.
implementation_evidence: Row numbers and corner stay pinned during horizontal scrolling.
validation_evidence: Chromium checks row-number left edge matches viewport after horizontal scroll.
limitations: Native reference comparison remains open.

requirements.title: Per-sheet scroll memory
requirements.source: 2026-10-19 user stress/scroll report and pasted UX audit
acceptance: Each sheet restores own horizontal/vertical offsets; newly created/imported sheet begins top-left; deleting a sheet cleans its view state.
implementation_evidence: Each sheet caches scroll axes and resized widths; Go to cell focus tokens are consumed once.
validation_evidence: Chromium graph/data unmount/remount restores both scroll axes and widths.
Final review regression: per-sheet active cell, anchor and rectangular selection now survive graph/data and other-sheet navigation independently of viewport position.
limitations: Session cache intentionally resets on page reload; persistence across application sessions is not implemented.

requirements.title: Scroll into empty cells
requirements.source: 2026-10-19 user stress/scroll report and pasted UX audit
acceptance: Continue into blank rows/columns within10000x30limits and type to materialize values; no need repeated Add row; bounds remain explicit.
implementation_evidence: Scrollable blank canvas extends to row10000 and columnAD; editing materializes cells.
validation_evidence: Chromium edited AD10000, saved, reloaded and checked exact value.
limitations: Advertised finite limits remain 10000 rows and30columns.

requirements.title: Fixed resizable column widths
requirements.source: 2026-10-19 user stress/scroll report and pasted UX audit
acceptance: Fixed default width does not stretch with window; drag handles resize specific columns without moving others unexpectedly; retain widths per sheet with declared persistence scope.
implementation_evidence: Columns start at112px and resize by header handles independently of viewport.
validation_evidence: Chromium resize changed actual width and restored it after switching sheets.
limitations: Widths are session view state, not saved workbook metadata.

acceptance: Zoom graph without changing scientific coordinates or exports; pan/scroll at high zoom; reset and accessible controls work in small windows.
implementation_evidence: Graph-only25–400% zoom controls, shortcuts, Ctrl-wheel, fit width and empty-space hand panning.
REA menu presets50/75/100/150/200/400/600/800/1000% implemented in plot-view.ts; zoom now reaches1000% without enlarging canvas backing above4x.
